title: Compensation for Loss or Damage Caused by Breach of Contract
summary: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew to be likely to result from breach. Remote and indirect losses are excluded.
verbatim_extract: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things...

title: Compensation for Breach of Contract where Penalty Stipulated
summary: When a contract contains a penalty clause or stipulated sum payable in case of breach, the aggrieved party is entitled to receive reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused.
verbatim_extract: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty...

title: Criteria for Giving Free Legal Services
summary: Every citizen who is a woman, child, member of Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe, industrial workman, disabled person, or person with income below the state threshold (typically Rs. 3 Lakhs per annum in most states) is entitled to free legal aid from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or NALSA.
verbatim_extract: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services under this Act if that person is... a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe... a woman or a child... a workman...

title: Organization of Lok Adalats
summary: State and District Legal Services Authorities organize Lok Adalats to determine and arrive at a compromise or settlement between parties for pending cases or pre-litigation disputes. Lok Adalat awards are final, binding, and involve zero court fees.
verbatim_extract: Every State Authority or District Authority... may organise Lok Adalats at such intervals and places... as it thinks fit...

title: General Limitation Period for Civil Suits and Claims
summary: Under the Limitation Act 1963, suits for recovery of money, return of security deposits, or breach of contract must generally be instituted within three years from the date when the right to sue or cause of action accrues.
verbatim_extract: Any suit for which no period of limitation is provided elsewhere in this Schedule: Three years from when the right to sue accrues.

title: Replacement of Indian Penal Code 1860 by BNS 2023
summary: On July 1, 2024, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) came into force, repealing the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC). NyayaSathi does not provide criminal defense advice or cite criminal offenses. All criminal concerns or physical threats must be escalated to law enforcement (Dial 112) or emergency helplines.
verbatim_extract: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 received assent of the President on December 25, 2023 and came into force on July 1, 2024, repealing Act 45 of 1860.
